A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same µPC research. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and complete Appendix A are readable and support comparison, including matching figures across renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original MNIST and Fashion-MNIST training results, learning-rate transfer experiments, Hessian analyses, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a CIFAR10 comparison using 128-layer networks.

M1.justification: The PC energy, residual architecture, layer scalings, and inference/learning procedures remain unchanged. V2 clarifies that µPC uses only some Depth-µP scalings; v1 already disclosed omitting Adam's prescribed learning-rate scaling. Table 1's width notation changes express equivalent scalings under the retained constant-width setup.

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR10 natural-image classification to the retained MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and toy-regression coverage. This is a bounded extension of dataset coverage using the same fully connected classification architecture, rather than an expansion to new architecture families or task types.

E2.justification: The corresponding existing comparisons retain standard PC, µPC, and BP with Depth-µP, alongside the existing initialization and inference-optimizer comparisons. CIFAR10 extends the same comparator set. The newly discussed Error Optimization method is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The added CIFAR10 comparison reports a 20-epoch evaluation of 128-layer residual ReLU networks, with learning rates transferred from 8-layer networks (Section 5 and Figure A.19). Existing experiments retain their reported budgets, model configurations, learning-rate searches, and inference procedures.

E4.justification: Section 7 newly reports that applying Depth-µP's prescribed Adam learning-rate scaling produced untrainable networks; v1 disclosed its omission without reporting this failure. This adds a qualitative scaling ablation. The existing activity-decay, initialization, optimizer, inference-step, and analytical-inference analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged: existing figures retain their seed counts and mean/standard-deviation displays, including five seeds for Figure A.17. The new CIFAR10 figure uses the existing three-seed reporting practice. No new statistical estimation or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: New Figure A.19 reports CIFAR10 accuracy reaching approximately 37% for µPC, 45% for BP with Depth-µP, and 10% for standard PC after 20 epochs. Section 7 also adds the qualitative failure of Adam learning-rate rescaling. Existing benchmark results and principal empirical trends are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 now explicitly assumes a randomly initialized linear ResNet, making its initialization restriction formal. Section 2.1 also specifies that O_n(1) means Θ_n(1), excluding vanishing activations. The underlying convergence argument, Hessian derivations, and convexity proof are substantially retained.

C1.justification: The main claims remain deep-PCN trainability, learning-rate transfer across width and depth, two scaling pathologies, and a conditional correspondence with BP. V2 emphasizes successful training outside the BP regime, but v1 already states this in Section 7 and Appendix A.1. CIFAR10 adds supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds an architectural explanation for weak CIFAR10 accuracy and explicitly argues that the adapted scalings are unlikely optimal. Section 7 connects recent gradient-decay findings to inference ill-conditioning, while Appendix A.3.6 sharpens the trainability/generalization distinction. Conversely, A.3.2 now incorrectly says an analytical nonlinear inference solution is available, contradicting Section 6.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 newly clarifies that the BP comparator employs the same scalings as µPC, without establishing a changed implementation. The JPC and experiment URLs, hardware, and general training details remain. V1's separate statement advertising analytical-inference and Hessian utilities is dropped, without establishing that those utilities were removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Goemaere et al.'s Error Optimization work and discusses its relationship to µPC in Section 7. It also adds Zucchet and Sacramento's work on implicit differentiation and equilibrium propagation, while removing Orvieto et al.'s Vanishing Curvature citation. The broader PC/µP positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 revises explanatory prose, especially Sections 6–7 and Appendix A.3.6, edits the abstract and background, and updates affiliations and publication headers. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially unchanged; these are localized revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds the CIFAR10 plot as Figure A.19 and gives the transfer plots numerical color scales and explicit logarithmic labels. Table 1 and several appendix figures move within the layout, with subsequent figure renumbering. Most existing graphical displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The CIFAR10 experiment usefully tests broader applicability while exposing a performance gap to BP. Explicit initialization assumptions, clearer comparator documentation, and numerical plot scales improve precision and interpretability. These limited gains outweigh the new contradictory sentence about nonlinear analytical inference in Appendix A.3.2. The central method and most evidence remain unchanged.
